headline: Saima Wazed resigns from WHO amid fraud probes
summary: Saima Wazed, daughter of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has stepped down from her role as WHO's Southeast Asia Regional Director following allegations of irregularities and fraud.
details: Saima Wazed, daughter of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, has resigned from her position as the Regional Director for the World Health Organization's (WHO) Southeast Asia Region. Her resignation comes amidst ongoing fraud probes and allegations of irregularities.
The allegations prompted an internal investigation within the global health body. Wazed had only recently assumed the high-profile role, having been elected in November of the previous year.

headline: Secret mobile phone data available for money, minister's private call details obtained
summary: An investigation revealed an active online market where personal mobile phone data, including call details, location, and messages, are sold for a fee, compromising the privacy of even high-profile individuals.
details: An alarming investigation has revealed that sensitive mobile phone data, including call details, messages, and location information, is readily available for purchase online in Bangladesh. This illicit trade operates through dedicated websites and social media platforms.

To verify the claims, Prothom Alo successfully obtained the Call Detail Records (CDR) of a minister by paying the requested fee. The minister confirmed the authenticity of the CDR, expressing shock and concern over the security implications.

The investigation further confirmed the widespread nature of this breach, as CDRs of two heads of critical IT and telecommunications agencies, along with two Prothom Alo employees, were also acquired and verified as accurate.

An extensive online market facilitates this data sale, with advertisements on Facebook, dedicated websites, and communication via Telegram and WhatsApp. For a fee, individuals can obtain national ID, CDR, location, SMS, TIN certificates, passport details, and mobile financial transaction records.

Prothom Alo previously gathered information on this issue in October. Separately, in August, verification firm Dismisslab published a report identifying 10 active websites and over 600 Facebook posts involved in selling personal data.

The compromised data includes not only call logs (who called whom, when, and for how long) but also the location of the mobile tower used during calls or SMS, and the device's IMEI number. This information is legally stored by mobile operators and accessible to law enforcement.
The managing director of Digitally Right, Miraj Ahmed Chowdhury, highlighted that such breaches violate personal privacy and could be exploited by criminal groups to track individuals' movements.
The cost for a three-month CDR is BDT 1,050, while a six-month record costs BDT 1,200. Operators of these websites often use WhatsApp groups to communicate with buyers.

Fakir Mahbub Anam, Minister of Post, Telecommunications and IT, stated that the government is actively working with BTRC and law enforcement to identify and prosecute those involved in this illegal data trade.

BTRC Chairman Major General (Retd.) Emdad Ul Bari echoed these concerns, emphasizing that the sale of citizens' personal data poses a significant risk to national security. BTRC is collaborating with law enforcement agencies to address the issue.
